title: The Readability Paradox: Why 'Simple' Fashion Images Win
lede: We looked at the save-ranked structure of 4,700 real outfit references: the most-saved images are not the most detailed. They are the most instantly readable. Here is why simplicity wins — and when it fails.
body_md:
## The paradox
Creators assume more detail equals more value. Our save-ranked library says otherwise: images with fewer competing elements outperform complex compositions in saves.

## Why readability beats detail
A viewer decides to save in roughly one second. In that window the brain processes one color story and one silhouette. A second competing element creates comparison — and comparison creates hesitation.

## The compression test
Describe any high-save image in three words: a color, a shape, a mood. If you can, it is readable. If you need a paragraph, it is over-composed.

## When simplicity fails
Readability is not emptiness. The winning formula is one strong idea plus supporting restraint — one statement accessory is fine, three is noise.

## The deeper lesson
AI makes infinite detail free — which makes restraint the scarce skill. Deciding what NOT to include is now more valuable than generating more.
